sources.entry: FinderGo - Open terminal quickly from Finder. [![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/onmyway133/FinderGo)
Finder Go - macOS app and Finder Sync Extension to open Terminal, iTerm, Hyper from Finder.

summary.one_liner: FinderGo is a macOS app and Finder Sync Extension that opens Terminal, iTerm, or Hyper at the current Finder folder.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes two ways to use it: a standalone macOS app that you drag into the Finder toolbar, and a Finder Sync Extension that adds a toolbar button in Finder. The app section says it currently supports iTerm. The default terminal can be switched by running a `defaults write` command for com.onmyway133.FinderGo with the value Terminal, iTerm, or Hyper. The Finder Sync Extension section lists Terminal, iTerm, and Hyper as supported. For the extension, the README says scripts must be copied into a sandbox Application Scripts folder using a curl command, and the extension must then be enabled under System Preferences > Extensions. The README states it supports macOS 10.12.
use_cases: open a terminal in the current Finder folder
add a terminal shortcut to the Finder toolbar
quickly jump from Finder to a shell
how_to_run: Download the binary from the release link in the README (link not included in the text provided).
Right-click the app to open it, since it is not from the App Store.
Cmd+Drag the app icon into the Finder toolbar.
Optionally run: defaults write com.onmyway133.FinderGo terminal iTerm (or Terminal or Hyper) to pick the default terminal.
For the Finder Sync Extension, run the curl command in the README to copy scripts into /Library/Application Scripts/com.onmyway133.FinderGo.FinderSyncExtension.
Enable FinderGo under System Preferences > Extensions > Finder, then Cmd+Drag it onto the Finder toolbar.
stack: Swift (implied by Xcode project structure; not named in README)
notable: Works as both a standalone app and a Finder Sync Extension
Default terminal is set with a defaults write command
caveats: The app is not from the App Store, so it must be opened via right-click on first launch.
The Finder Sync Extension needs scripts copied into a sandbox folder, which is a manual setup step.
The standalone app section says it supports only iTerm for now.
